# Composing results

## Overview
`ems_compose()` retrieves and processes results from a solved model run.
Results are parsed and filtered according to the `which` argument.
Data validation and consistency checks are performed during the parsing process.

By default, [`ems_solve()`](solve.qmd) calls `ems_compose()` automatically, so this function is primarily used when `suppress_outputs = TRUE` was passed to [`ems_solve()`](solve.qmd) or [`solve_in_situ()`](solve.qmd), or when re-parsing results from a previous run.

```r
ems_compose(
  cmf_path,
  which = "all",
  passes = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `cmf_path` | | Path to the CMF file generated by [`ems_deploy()`](deploy.qmd) |
| `which` | `"all"` | `"all"` returns every model variable and coefficient (coefficients at their updated, post-simulation values), except the condensation coefficients (`CSUB<n>`, see [Condensation coefficients](model_load.qmd#csub)), which come back only when named. Otherwise, a character vector of variable and coefficient names to retrieve, matched without regard to case |
| `passes` | `FALSE` | `TRUE` adds the separate solutions of a three-pass `"Gragg"`, `"Midpoint"` or `"Euler"` run and their accuracy (see [Separate solutions](#passes)) |

## Basic usage

After a standard model run with suppressed outputs:
```r
ems_solve(
  cmf_path = cmf_path,
  solution_method = "Gragg",
  matrix_method = "LU",
  suppress_outputs = TRUE
)

# Parse all results
outputs <- ems_compose(cmf_path = cmf_path)
```

## Filtering output

Pass a character vector of names to `which` to retrieve a subset of results.
Variables and coefficients can be mixed freely in a single call:

```r
# All model variables and coefficients (default)
all_outputs <- ems_compose(cmf_path = cmf_path)

# Single variable by name
qfd <- ems_compose(cmf_path = cmf_path, which = "qfd")

# Single coefficient by name
SAVE <- ems_compose(cmf_path = cmf_path, which = "SAVE")

# Multiple names with mixed variables and coefficients
results <- ems_compose(cmf_path = cmf_path, which = c("qfd", "qfm", "SAVE"))
```

Note that some coefficient names differ from their associated HAR headers.
For example, the coefficient exposed as `"VTMFSD"` corresponds to the `VTWR` header.
Use the name as it appears in the model file, not the header.

## Return value

`ems_compose()` returns a tibble with one row per result and four columns:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `name` | Variable or coefficient name as it appears in the model file |
| `label` | Description string from the model file |
| `type` | `"variable"`, `"coefficient"` or `"postsim"` (coefficients computed in a `PostSim` section) |
| `dat` | List-column of data.tables, one per row, containing the result values |

## Levels results {#levels}

A variable declared with `ORIG_LEVEL=` in the model file has a known pre-simulation level: either a coefficient over exactly the variable's sets (GTAP's `qfd` takes `VDFB`, its value at base prices) or a number (`1.0` for a price index).
Levels variables know theirs too.
For these variables the data.table gains:

| Column | Percent-change variable | Change variable |
|--------|-------------------------|-----------------|
| `pre_level` | pre-simulation level | pre-simulation level |
| `post_level` | `pre_level * (1 + Value / 100)` | `pre_level + Value` |
| `change` / `percent_change` | `change`: the ordinary change | `percent_change`: the percent change |

For runs solved with `"BoSha32"` or `"DoPri54"` (see [solving](solve.qmd)), each variable's data.table also has an `error_estimate` column.
Sort it in descending order to find the least settled results; it is an indicator, not a bound on the error.

## Separate solutions {#passes}

A three-pass `"Gragg"`, `"Midpoint"` or `"Euler"` run extrapolates from three solutions with increasing step counts (see [solving](solve.qmd)).
`passes = TRUE` returns them, so the accuracy of each result can be inspected:

```r
outputs <- ems_compose(cmf_path, passes = TRUE)
attr(outputs, "accuracy")
```

Each variable's data.table gains:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `pass1`, `pass2`, `pass3` | The solutions with the fewest to the most steps, in the units of `Value` |
| `figures` | Significant figures to which the two two-pass extrapolations agree (0 to 6; `NA` for a result judged zero, both extrapolations below 1e-6) |
| `levels_figures` | The same for the variable's levels value, which a percent-change result usually has more of |
| `error` | The difference between the two extrapolations, in the units of `Value` |
| `code` | The convergence code of GEMPACK manual 26.2.3, for example `"CX"` (confidence in the extrapolated result) or `"MD!"` (monotonic but appearing to diverge) |
| `summarized` | Whether the element counts in the run's accuracy summary: `TRUE` for endogenous and backsolved results (of the `accuracy_vars` variables when those are given), `FALSE` for exogenous elements, whose values the shock sets |

The `accuracy` attribute has one row per variable: `elements`, `summarized`, the lowest figures (`min_figures`, `min_levels_figures`; a result judged zero counts as 6), the share of results at `accuracy_figures` or more (`share_figures`, `share_levels_figures`; see [options](options.qmd)), `worst_code` and `max_error`.
With subintervals, `figures` and `levels_figures` are the lowest over the subintervals and `code` the worst; the pass columns and `error` come from the last subinterval alone, each pass compounded onto the extrapolated result of the subintervals before it.
A run that wrote no separate solutions stops with an error.
